original_question: Determine whether there exists an existential inclusion of L(F2) into MU, and whether the random embedding is existential in the Haar-sampling sense.
target_in_paper: Section "Existential embeddings", Problem 13: "Does there exist an existential inclusion of L(F_2) into M^U? Is the random embedding existential, in the sense of Haar-sampling?"
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact target. It names the correct source factor L(F_2), the correct target M^U, the correct property (existential inclusion), and it preserves the paper's second clause about the Haar-sampled random embedding. In substance, it is almost a paraphrase of Problem 13.
missing_details: The paper fixes U once and for all as a nonprincipal ultrafilter on N in its opening notation; your draft does not say that.
M^U should be defined explicitly as the tracial matrix ultraproduct ∏_{n→U} M_n(C); otherwise the ambient target algebra is not stand-alone.
To avoid ambiguity, one should say that L(F_2) is the group von Neumann algebra of the free group F_2 on two generators.

The phrase "existential inclusion" should be unpacked using the paper's definition: an embedding ι:N→M is existential if there exists an embedding θ:M→N^U such that θ∘ι is the diagonal embedding of N into N^U.
The ambient category should be made explicit: the problem is about embeddings of tracial von Neumann algebras / II_1 factors over C.

The paper's phrase "the random embedding" is informal; to make the question fully stand-alone one must specify that this refers to the embedding produced by Haar-sampling matrix-level images of the free generators in the matrix factors entering the ultraproduct.

The paper does not state the probability qualifier for the random clause, so a fully explicit stand-alone version must decide whether the intended meaning is almost sure existentiality, positive-probability existentiality, or some other probabilistic interpretation.
refined_question: Fix a nonprincipal ultrafilter U on N, let M^U := ∏_{n→U} M_n(C) be the tracial matrix ultraproduct, and let L(F_2) denote the group von Neumann algebra of the free group on two generators. Does there exist an embedding ι:L(F_2)→M^U that is existential, in the sense that there exists an embedding θ:M^U→L(F_2)^U such that θ∘ι is the diagonal embedding of L(F_2) into L(F_2)^U? Moreover, for the Haar-sampled random embedding of L(F_2) into M^U alluded to in the paper, is that embedding existential?
justification: This is exactly Problem 13 in the paper's section on existential embeddings, so it is the nearest official formulation and should not be broadened to neighboring questions about other existential copies or other target factors. The global notation needed to make the question stand-alone is fixed in the opening paragraph: U is a nonprincipal ultrafilter on N and M^U is the tracial matrix ultraproduct. The definition of an existential embedding is given immediately at the start of the "Existential embeddings" section. The only real incompleteness in your draft is that these notational and model-theoretic conventions are left implicit, and the paper's second clause about the "random embedding" remains informal even in the original text. The paper gives no explicit equivalent reformulation of Problem 13, so none should be added.
